text: If ever a man and his wife, or a man and his mistress, who pass nights as well as days together, absolutely lay aside all good-breeding, their intimacy will soon degenerate into a coarse familiarity, infallibly productive of contempt or disgust.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter LXXXVIII, to his son, London, November 3, Old Style 1749
